My professional work focuses on applied research, data science, and program evaluation, primarily in community mental health. I use statistical methods and data to investigate questions about service delivery, workforce experiences, and organizational outcomes. Measurement is also important to this work, especially when deciding what data can tell us and how to interpret the results.

## Research and evaluation

I serve as Director of Research and Evaluation at Didi Hirsch Mental Health Services. My work includes applied studies, program evaluation, data analysis, outcome and assessment measures, data quality, and reporting findings to people who use them to make decisions.

I am particularly interested in how organizations can use existing data more effectively, and in the methodological choices that affect the conclusions we draw from that data.

## Education and quantitative methods

I earned an **M.A. in Psychology with an emphasis in Quantitative Methods** from California State University, Fullerton, and a **B.A. in Psychology** with a minor in Philosophy from California State University, Dominguez Hills.

My interests include statistical modeling, psychological measurement, research methodology, and applied data analysis.

## Teaching and research project guidance

Since 2016, I have provided periodic guidance on the annual applied research or evaluation projects completed by doctoral psychology interns at Didi Hirsch Mental Health Services. I meet with interns to discuss the project and provide additional feedback when needed. This is a limited, project-focused responsibility within my research role rather than a formal college teaching appointment.

I am also building learning resources in statistics and research methods. The [Teaching & Learning section](teaching.qmd) is organized to accommodate multiple courses, short lectures, videos, and independent activities as those materials become available.

## Research and collaboration

My scholarly interests include mental health services, workforce experiences, treatment engagement, and applied evaluation.
